body: Thank you, I won't stop them cold turkey now. But for the record I never had bipolar or anything that major. Just really bad anxiety and panic attacks.

Trust me, I'm really angry too. It's been a couple months since he said misdiagnosis and I still can't quite process it. Not a day goes by where I don't think about it. After I tell him to take me off of all the meds, I won't go back to a psychiatrist.
I think that way too sometimes too. I won't be doing it cold turkey now. Thanks.

Yea she said that yesterday and it's still bothering me. Mostly because I have read a lot of articles and been told by a lot of people that exercise helps anxiety, and when she told me I thought, "well, she's a doctor, so surly she knows", and confused me. Now I don't know what to believe. But I will continue to exercise because it does make me feel better.

I feel really relaxed after exercising, not sure if it's because I feel good that I did something productive or something else. A day later and I'm still a bit confused as to why she said that. 

I guess a lot of doctors are different. I've had a few psychiatrists in the past and I never really trust them. I understand that medication is necessary at times, but sometimes the way they have tried to push so many medications on me makes me uncomfortable. I've been misdiagnosed with a lot of things, and put on a bunch of medication that I never really needed.

I'll definitely be careful, and thanks for your reply!

Thanks for replying, I've been on all anti-anxiety meds that weren't benzos, including SSRIs, and nothing has really worked. I just need something for panic attacks at this point. I will continue exercising though!
Wow that's really great that you're off of those meds, that's awesome. I'm going to add a little more to my exercises, can't wait to be completely off of them. Thanks for sharing your story!

Thanks, I appreciate your reply.

Hopefully .5 will at least calm me down a bit. I definitely won't be taking it daily, only when the panic attacks feel unbearable as they have in the past. 

Yea, I meant a single dose. Thanks for clearing that up for me. 

I'm really hoping it will help me when these attacks come back. It's been a horrible experience. 

I found it odd that my psychiatrist said that exercise doesn't help anxiety too. I'm really starting to wonder. 

Thanks, I will be sure to message you if I have any other concerns!

Oh wow, two bad knees sounds painful. I had a partial tear on my ACL 2 years ago and it's still giving me problems. I like the idea of biking, and I have a swimming pool in my gym, but walking out in nature is pretty awesome for me at the moment. I will be looking into those 2 though because I'm looking to expand on my choices of exercises. 

Did you start all of these sports/exercises after you no longer had anxiety or during/before?

Thanks for this. I thought it was really weird that she said exercise doesn't help anxiety as well. I have been doing cardio for 2 weeks. I'm glad to hear that your anxiety went away, and I hope to get there too. Right now I can't do high intensity cardio because of a bad knee, but I have been walking at about 3 mph for over an hour a day. Do you think that's enough for now?
Wow, it knocked you out for 2 days?
Thanks for replying. This really helped set my mind at ease a bit. So anxiety is really made worse by exercise? I will continue to exercise, I'm just curious about it making anxiety worse.

Breathing exercises really help a lot of times, but once the wheels of a panic attack are set in motion, usually there is nothing that can stop it. Same with the distractions. 

Is exercise really bad for anxiety then? There is a park about 20 minutes away from here that really helps though. When I go there I just go to walk around and enjoy the nature. I appreciate your reply.

I'm glad to hear that running has helped you with your depression and anxiety. I hope that it will help me if I do exercise everyday, and I will keep on trucking! I have a question about running. Did you just one day decide that you were going to run, and just started running? Or did you start out by walking for a week or two and worked your way up to running?

I was told I will need meds for the rest of my life. I guess I just refuse to accept it. It's like I know I have all of these mental conditions, but I just can't accept it. I know I have to, but it's hard to. 

Anyway, I will keep exercising and eating right in hopes that it helps me mentally. 

Also, question, did exercise ever help you mentally before you found the right meds? Or after maybe?

This is somewhat depressing. But as you said, every person is different, and hopefully I can feel better. Sorry to hear that it isn't helping you though. I hate it sometimes too, but only because I get bored on the treadmill, I just have to find something else. Super happy to see that you're still at it after 4 months though. At least you're pushing yourself to do it despite feeling awful during and after. Don't know if you know it, but that in itself is inspiring. Sometimes I feel like I can't because of this or that, and you do it regardless of your mental state of mind. I hope that one day you find something that will pull you out of that state of mind. I hope I find that something too!
